narrative.overview: FluidMusic is a quiet listening instrument embedded in Hermes Desktop: deep navy carries the workspace, cool graphite separates compact chrome, and sparse coral and violet signals make state readable without turning the surface into a branded streaming clone. The system inherits Hermes typography and semantic --ui-* variables so it remains native to the host while keeping a recognisable Night Radio hierarchy. The signature object is Orbit: a large circular artwork or record field in the now-playing band. It supplies one memorable silhouette while the rest of the interface stays operational—compact Blackstage-style navigation, hairline divisions, aligned metadata, honest provider labels, and dense rows. Runtime provider artwork may fill Orbit and media tiles; no raster artwork, texture, or decorative image asset ships with the plugin.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy and cool graphite structure with off-white text.
Coral reserved for live/broadcast emphasis and the active navigation underline.
Violet used for provider/source identity and selected secondary tabs.
One circular Orbit focal object; other components remain compact and rectilinear.
Four stable primary destinations: Browse, Library, Queue, and Settings.
Provider capabilities and ownership stay visible instead of being visually normalised away.
Theme-aware surfaces derive from Hermes semantic variables; green-tinted backgrounds are forbidden.

rules.name: The No-Green-Background Rule
rules.body: Never tint workspace, card, tile, chip, or selected-state backgrounds green. Spotify remains identifiable through copy, icons, and violet source treatment—not a green wash.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Coral means live or active; violet means source or secondary selection. Do not use either as broad decorative fill.

rules.name: The Semantic Host Rule
rules.body: Base surfaces, text, strokes, focus, and control accent come from Hermes --ui-* variables. Fixed brand accents supplement the host; they do not replace its theme contract.

rules.name: The Inherited Voice Rule
rules.body: Do not ship a custom font for FluidMusic. Inherit Hermes typography so the plugin belongs to the desktop shell.

rules.name: The Tight-Title Rule
rules.body: Tight negative tracking is for display, page, and section titles only. Body copy and controls retain normal tracking.

rules.name: The Stable-Destinations Rule
rules.body: Browse, Library, Queue, and Settings remain the only primary workspace destinations; source choices belong in secondary tabs.

rules.name: The One-Player Rule
rules.body: The now-playing band owns the full workspace playback story. Never add a bottom player bar.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Panels and rows use borders and tonal shifts at rest. Shadows are reserved for Orbit, popovers, dialogs, and inset state markers.

rules.name: The One-Circle Rule
rules.body: Orbit is the dominant circle. Do not turn every control, chip, tile, or card into a pill or disc.

dos: Do build every surface from Hermes semantic variables plus the fixed coral and violet signals.
Do keep Orbit as the single memorable focal object and let runtime artwork supply its content.
Do preserve all four primary destinations and use secondary tabs for provider or section changes.
Do render controls from active-source capabilities and state the provider/device boundary in copy.
Do distinguish editable local collections from read-only legacy mixes through labels, notices, and available actions.
Do test broad, 980px, 720px, and 390px container behavior, visible focus, keyboard dismissal, and reduced motion.
donts: Don't use green-tinted backgrounds, Spotify-green panels, or provider-colored page washes.
Don't add a sidebar-plus-bottom-player streaming shell or duplicate the now-playing controls in a footer.
Don't ship raster artwork, texture, or placeholder imagery; provider artwork is runtime content and SVG supplies fallbacks.
Don't show fake seek, previous, next, shuffle, repeat, queue, or device actions where the active source cannot perform them.
Don't make new saved collections cross-source; use temporary Up Next for mixed listening and preserve legacy mixes as read-only.
Don't replace hairline structure with stacks of floating cards, broad shadows, excessive pills, or decorative animation.
